title: Advanced Serverless Architectures & EventBridge
exp: Architect enterprise AWS serverless applications using Lambda Provisioned Concurrency, EventBridge Pipes, DynamoDB Single-Table Design, and SQS DLQ handling.
pts: **Lambda Execution Lifecycle:** Cold starts vs Warm starts; Provisioned Concurrency for zero cold start SLA.
**EventBridge Pipes:** point-to-point integration connecting sources (DynamoDB Streams, SQS, Kinesis) to targets (Step Functions, Lambda, EventBus) with built-in filtering & enrichment.
**DynamoDB Single-Table Design:** modeling multiple entity types in a single table using generic `PK` / `SK` and Global Secondary Indexes (GSIs).
**Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) & Lambda Event Source Mapping:** max retry attempts, bisect on function error, failure destination.

qa.q: Why use EventBridge Pipes instead of writing custom Lambda functions for event filtering and transformation?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** EventBridge Pipes provides built-in, serverless point-to-point integration with zero custom code, filtering and enriching events in-transit between SQS/DynamoDB Streams and downstream targets, reducing Lambda execution costs and maintenance.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Operating Why use EventBridge Pipes instead of writing custom Lambda functions for event filtering and transformation? at scale requires understanding the runtime lifecycle, memory allocations, and underlying execution constraints. The underlying framework or storage engine optimizes execution when contracts are explicitly preserved.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Un-handled edge cases in Why use EventBridge Pipes instead of writing custom Lambda functions for event filtering and transformation? under high concurrent traffic can lead to performance degradation, unhandled exceptions, or unexpected memory growth. Always enforce defensive validation and error handling.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Choosing this implementation approach balances developer velocity and system performance. Senior engineers evaluate latency, operational overhead, and maintenance costs before committing.

qa.q: What are the trade-offs of DynamoDB Single-Table Design versus Multi-Table Design?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Single-table design minimizes HTTP connection overhead and enables fetching related entities (User + Orders) in one network request (Query). Trade-off: high design complexity, steep learning curve, inflexible ad-hoc query capabilities without creating new GSIs.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** EF Core builds an Expression Tree, translates it via the relational SQL provider into a parameterized T-SQL query, and materializes entities into the DbContext Change Tracker. N+1 queries occur when navigating un-included navigation properties in a loop.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Executing queries without AsNoTracking() in read-only APIs forces EF Core to keep snapshot copies of all returned entities in memory, causing high RAM usage and CPU tracking overhead.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** AsNoTracking() speeds up read queries by 20-30% and reduces memory footprint, but disables identity resolution and automatic change tracking for updates.
